title: HarnessProfile
description: Declarative runtime profile governing on-the-fly skill rendering, worker launch, the machine's harness scan and probes, activity and usage mapping, and bundle generation.

equals.description: null: the variable is present with any value; a string: it has exactly this value.

pointer_or_na.description: A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into a line of the output stream; null: the harness does not report the figure; the string not_applicable: the figure does not exist for this harness by design.

args.description: Argument templates appended for this class, with the slots of argv.

tool_set.description: enforced: the harness limits the worker to the tools of its role. advisory: the harness cannot limit a worker's tools; the worker runs with every tool of the harness, and the role's tool set only tells it which to use.

schema_version.description: Version of the harness profile schema.

harness_id.description: Canonical identifier of the harness; equal to the file name of the profile. The set of clients is the set of profiles.

icon.description: The harness's icon (Harness Icons below); null: the generated monogram.

source.description: For form source: the URL of the maker's official icon file, fetched once by the runtime on the operator's consent.

bundled.description: For form bundled: the name of an icon shipped in the binary.

tools.description: Mapping of abstract harness capabilities to runtime-specific tool names and parameter idioms.

mode.description: Primary mechanism used by the model to load vocabulary skills.

load_directive_template.description: Template rendered when a skill references another skill (e.g. 'pm_skill(uri="{{uri}}")').

skills_extension.description: true once the harness's support of the MCP Skills Extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/skills) is verified; the bundle of such a harness installs no shim skill (harness-integration/02-bundle-manifest.adoc, Shim Skill).

headless.description: Launch contract of the harness's headless CLI for workers (job kind llm); null for a harness without a headless run, which is shown and never enrolled for workers. Nothing is installed: the server composes every launch per worker.

executable.description: Name of the harness CLI; the operator enrols its absolute path per machine (the onboarding's harness.enrol, or pm-operator enrol-harness), never looked up through PATH at launch.

install_locations.description: Directories the harness scan searches for the executable beside the directories of the operator's login PATH; ~ is the home directory, {app_dir} the platform's application directories (Harness Scan below).

install_hint.description: Message key of the text that tells the operator how to install the harness, shown where the scan did not find it.

auth_probe.description: The login probe (Login Probe below); null: the harness is probed by one minimal headless call of its launch, whose token cost is shown before it runs.

login_command.description: The harness's own login command, shown to the operator when logged out; never run by the runtime.

models_probe.description: The models probe (Model Tiers below); null: the harness cannot list its models, and the operator enters their ids.

pointer.description: For format json: the JSON Pointer to the array of model ids; null for lines.

weights_probe.description: How the identity of a model's weights is read (Endpoint Harness, Weights Identity); null: the harness reports none, and its model name stands for its weights.

model_tiers.description: The model each tier of the shipped default assignment maps to on this harness (Model Tiers below); null: the harness has no model of that tier.

supported_versions.description: Version range of the harness CLI (for example '>=2.1.0 <3.0.0'), probed with identity.version_probe; a self-updated harness is probed only after its update_evidence passed, then accepted and audited inside the range, and outside it every worker launch is refused harness_version_unsupported.

update_evidence.description: How a changed executable of this harness is shown to be the vendor's, without running it (Update Evidence below).

method.description: code_signature: the platform code signature of the executable is valid and names signer. package_provenance: the package manager that installed it verifies the package's signed provenance and the executable is the package's file. none: no check; every change waits for the operator's enrolment.

signer.description: For code_signature, the signer identity the signature must name (on macOS the Developer ID team identifier); for package_provenance, the source repository the provenance must name; null for none.

agent_mode.description: inline: the server renders a per-worker named agent definition into the {{agent}} slot (claude: --agents JSON; opencode: agent in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT); flags: the launch is composed by per-call flags only (codex).

argv.description: Argument-vector template after the executable. Each item is a literal or contains typed slots of the closed set {{prompt_file}}, {{model}}, {{effort}}, {{mcp_config}}, {{result_schema}}, {{tools}}, {{cwd}}, {{agent}}, {{shim_dir}}; a slot whose value is absent for the job removes its item.

mcp_config.description: How a worker of this harness receives the MCP configuration that starts its job relay.

delivery.description: slot: the server renders the configuration into the {{mcp_config}} slot of argv or env. file: the server writes it to path before the launch, and no template uses the slot.

path.description: For delivery file: the file the harness reads, relative to the worker's working directory (antigravity: .agents/mcp_config.json); null for delivery slot.

exclusive.description: true: the harness connects to no MCP server but the one of this configuration. false: it also connects to the servers of its own configuration files.

classes.description: What the harness can run per role class (Role Classes below). A class that is null is not runnable on this harness: a role artifact of that class naming it is invalid with reason harness_class_not_runnable.

zero_tool.description: The class of the screener and the judge. Non-null only for a harness that can be started with no tool at all, no MCP connection, and its project and user settings off.

args.description: Argument templates appended for this class, with the slots of argv.

env.description: Environment variables the launch sets, with the same slots (for example OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: '{{agent}}'); PM_MCP_JOB_TOKEN and PM_MCP_JOB_ID are set by the server and never declared here. Never a harness authentication variable: the harness uses its own login.

inline_settings.description: Harness-native settings the server merges into the inline configuration document it renders into {{agent}}, beside the agent and the MCP configuration (Inline Settings below); a key {{provider}} is replaced by the provider of the worker's model, the part before its first '/'. null for a harness without such a document (claude, antigravity, codex).

capabilities.description: Declared capabilities of the headless run that the server adapts to (result parsing, session residue, usage and cost recording, exit handling, settings control). extension_isolation: the launch of the writer and read_only classes loads the project's instruction files, no instruction file or skill of the user, and no plugin, hook, or MCP server from any settings file (Role Classes below). project_skill_isolation: that launch loads no skill directory of the project and loads the shim skill from {{shim_dir}} (Role Classes below). Only project_settings_control and extension_isolation take part in whether a class is runnable, through the rules of Role Classes.

model_efforts.description: Effort values the harness accepts per model, in ascending order; key * applies to every model without its own entry; an empty list means the model takes no effort flag. A role artifact's effort is checked against it on load (model-work/01-roles-and-configuration.adoc).

result_pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the structured result in the final output; null: the result is parsed from the final message against the result schema, fail-closed.

usage.description: JSON Pointers into the harness output for each usage figure, read per turn (Tokens, Not Money below), with the accumulation of the figures they point to; null: not reported by the harness (recorded unmeasured, reason not_reported_by_harness); not_applicable: the figure does not exist for this harness by design (recorded not_applicable, counted 0). Each pointer fills the metrics-row column of the same name, except cache_read -> cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation -> cache_creation_input_tokens, and reasoning -> reasoning_tokens. There is no pointer for the total: total_tokens is derived (the sum of the five token components, a not-applicable one counting 0, when every applicable one is measured, otherwise unmeasured). input_tokens, output_tokens and tool_uses are never not_applicable.

cost_usd.description: Recorded data only: never shown, never summed into a figure the operator sees, never read by a rule.

model.description: JSON Pointer to the identifier of the model the harness reports for the turn; fills served_models of the metrics row. Recorded and shown only (The Model That Answered below); null: not reported (served_models recorded unmeasured).

accumulation.description: What the token and tool-use figures of a turn line are: per_turn, the figures of that turn alone; running_total, the totals of the worker's run so far, which the runtime turns into the turn's own figures (Tokens, Not Money below).

events.description: The mapping of a line of the output stream onto the closed activity kinds (What a Worker Does below); null: the harness's output gives no event stream (output.format json), and its tasks show only the server's own entries.

kind_pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the field that tells a line's kind.

kinds.description: Per activity kind the values of kind_pointer that map to it, with the pointers of its fields.

target.description: Pointers tried in order for the target: a path, a command line, a server link with its id; never the whole arguments.

stop_reason.description: Pointer to the turn's stop reason; null: the harness's output does not carry it.

turn.description: Its usage is read through the usage pointers; its stop reason through stop_reason.

loaded.description: The line of the output stream in which the harness reports what a worker loaded at its start, checked at every start of a writer or read_only worker (What a Worker Loaded below); null: the harness gives no such line, and only the stage isolation measures what its workers load.

match_pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the field that identifies the line.

match.description: The values of match_pointer that identify the line.

plugins.description: Pointer to the array of the loaded plugins.

plugin_name.description: Pointer, relative to an element of plugins, to its name.

mcp_servers.description: Pointer to the array of the MCP servers of the run.

mcp_server_name.description: Pointer, relative to an element of mcp_servers, to its name.

tools.description: Pointer to the array of the names of the tools offered to the model.

expected_plugins.description: The plugins the stage isolation found in a launch of the class without decoys: those built into the harness version.

endpoints.description: The host:port destinations a worker of this harness needs (its model provider, its login refresh), the only ones its egress proxy admits (Job Runtime Specification, Worker Egress Proxy); measured by the egress stage of the profile verification.

writable_paths.description: Home-relative sub-paths a headless harness must write to run (its login or credential file, caches, the session directory, its own state file), added to the write set of a worker. Never a harness home as a whole and never a settings, skill, or command file that the bundle manifest manages; profile validation refuses such an entry. Empty for a harness whose writes all go to its per-worker data home.

readable_paths.description: Home-relative paths a headless harness must read to run beyond its installation, its writable paths, and the files its bundle manifest manages, added to the read set of a worker (Job Runtime Specification, Worker Read Set). Never the home directory and never an entry that equals, contains, or lies in a credential location; profile validation refuses such an entry. Measured by the paths stage of the profile verification.

data_home.description: Per-worker data home, for a harness whose local state is one per-user store shared by all its processes; null: the harness needs none. The runtime points variable at the worker's own data directory below its job-private directory and copies login_file into it (job-runtime, Per-Worker Data Home).

variable.description: The environment variable that relocates the harness's data directory (opencode: XDG_DATA_HOME); never a credential-pattern name.

login_file.description: The harness's own login file, relative to the data directory the variable relocates (opencode: opencode/auth.json); copied byte for byte with mode 0600, never parsed, stored, or logged.

tool_result_limit_chars.description: The largest tool result, in characters, the harness passes to its model whole; null: the harness passed every size the stage limits offered whole, and the server applies no limit. The server returns no larger tool result to a worker of this harness: it sends identifiers and links first and the rest as parts read as resources (model-work, Offer). A non-null value requires a non-empty resource_tools.

resource_tools.description: Names of the harness's tools that list and read MCP resources; the server adds them to the tool set of the writer and read_only classes, never of zero_tool. Empty: the harness offers none, and its jobs read no resources.

session_residue.description: ephemeral: the launch always passes the harness's no-persistence flag; persisted: the harness keeps session files, reported in both clients.

resumability.description: Whether a worker of this harness can continue after its question (Resumability below); set only from profile verification, every form not measured is false or null.

hold.description: A worker holds its task in pm_wait until the answer and continues in the same context.

max_hold_seconds.description: The longest hold measured on the harness; a role's hold_seconds above it is cut to it. null when hold is false.

resume.description: A worker ends with its session stored and a new generation resumes it with the answer; null: not possible or not measured.

argv.description: The launch arguments that resume a stored session; exactly one item holds {{session_id}}. The rest of the launch (env, mcp_config, the class's args) is the role's normal launch without the no-persistence flag.

session_id.description: JSON Pointer into the worker's structured result to its session id.

max_age_seconds.description: The oldest stored session measured to resume with its context.

context_budget_tokens.description: Harness fallback of the context budget of a worker, used only for a role artifact that does not set context_budget_tokens (Model Work, Role Artifact Schema); the per-envelope packing budget is derived from the effective value (Model Work, Envelopes), compiled fallback 400000 when neither sets it, operator override envelope_budget_tokens in local-config.json; this fallback and the compiled one are capped at the model's long_context_thresholds entry.

long_context_thresholds.description: Per model id of this harness, the input tokens above which its provider bills a request at the model's long-context price (Model Tiers below); a fallback of the context budget is capped at it, a role artifact's own context_budget_tokens is not.

worker.description: Worker parameters and eligibility of the harness (Worker Block below). While eligible is false, every value other than eligible is null or a value measured on the harness, and none of them has an effect.

eligible.description: Whether the harness may host workers; true only after its worker behaviour has been measured on it under the target conditions with every fault of the fault matrix passed, and only with a non-null headless block.

restricted_models.description: Model identifiers of this harness that accept an enforced tool set; * stands for every model, <provider>/* for every model of that provider. A role of a class whose tool_set is enforced naming another model of this harness is invalid; null on a harness with no enforced class.

ack_deadline_seconds.description: Time from an offer to its acknowledgement after which the supervisor ends the worker; with ack_informational it equals the silence limit.

ack_informational.description: true: a missing acknowledgement ends no worker; silence alone decides.

silence_grace_seconds.description: Time beyond the bounded wait without an open wait call or any other call after which the supervisor ends the worker.

idle_wakeups.description: Consecutive wait answers without a task after which a warm worker is recycled.

detection.description: How the operator checks of pm-operator recognise a coding agent's environment (Harness Integration Table); null for a harness whose environment carries no signal. Read by the profile reader of pm-api.

precedence.description: Position in the fixed detection order when the primary signals of several harnesses are present and no process marker decides; lower wins. Unique across the profiles.

primary_signals.description: Any one of them present detects the harness.

secondary_signals.description: Signals that support a detection and never establish one.

process_markers.description: Variables holding a process id of the harness; among several detected harnesses the one whose marker names the nearest ancestor process wins (Nested harnesses).

ai_agent_prefixes.description: Prefixes of AI_AGENT (before the first _ or @) that map to this harness, as a secondary signal.

reaches.description: The processes that see the signals: command (a command the harness runs through its shell tool, such as pm-operator) and serve (an MCP server the harness starts).

identity.description: The version probe of the harness (Harness Identity Probes), run by the harness scan, the enrolment, a worker's spawn, and the profile verification. With detection it forms the harness-detection table of pm-api.

version_probe.description: Argument vector printing the exact harness build; run without a shell and with a bounded timeout; null when the harness offers none.

version_pattern.description: Regular expression with one capture group extracting the harness version from the probe's standard output; null iff version_probe is null.
